key_insight: MeanFlowNFT extends forward-process reinforcement learning to MeanFlow generators, enabling them to be aligned with human preferences and task goals while preserving their fast few-step sampling advantage. The key idea is to optimize average-velocity generators directly, without relying on expensive reverse-process trajectories.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of applying efficient RL-based alignment methods, originally designed for diffusion/flow models, to MeanFlow generators. It tackles the challenge of improving generator behavior using forward-process signals alone, without likelihood estimation or reverse-time sampling.
method: Builds on DiffusionNFT-style forward-process RL to adapt the training paradigm to MeanFlow's average-velocity formulation.
Uses forward trajectories and reward signals to guide model updates, avoiding reverse-process rollouts.
Aligns generation with external objectives while keeping sampling efficient and few-step friendly.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical way to align fast generative models with preferences or downstream tasks without sacrificing inference speed. It broadens RL-based alignment beyond diffusion models to a more efficient generation family.

paper_title: MeanFlowNFT: Bringing Forward-Process RL to Average-Velocity Generators
paper_authors: Yushi Huang, Xiangxin Zhou, Jun Zhang, Liefeng Bo, Tianyu Pang
